title: Where agent discretion ends
rec: Claude and Codex reason every question from the philosophy and recommend; they never pick a language answer through code, fixtures, diagnostics or docs. 'Important' = anything that revises a decided rule, changes observable language meaning you have not ruled on, or that you reserved. Every important decision comes to you.
why: Codex: the word 'important' was undefined, which could let agents treat language decisions as routine.

title: Priority order when principles conflict
rec: Soundness and provability > transparency (with auditability, honest trust boundaries and compiler-owned identity) > one authoritative definition (checked derived views allowed) > explicitness at the use site > brevity. The philosophy guides open choices and never silently reopens decided rules.
why: This order is what moved Q5 to explicit capability arguments. Codex required auditability, trust boundaries and identity to stay load-bearing.

title: Lean is the spec: confirm the amendment
rec: Confirm that 'no prose generated from Lean' amends the earlier written commitment to generated chapters. Keep a browsable rendering of the Lean itself (Lean's doc tool) plus coverage checks; a prose chapter retires only once its rules are fully covered.
why: You decided this today; Codex asked that the amendment to the earlier contract be explicit.
revises: Generated-chapter requirement (philosophy rule 6 / earlier roadmap commitment): replaced by one normative Lean file with doc comments and examples, a browsable rendering of that Lean, and coverage-gated retirement of prose chapters; your decision of 2026-11-04

title: Duplicate enum variants or methods (bug 313)
rec: Refuse duplicate variant names in one enum and duplicate method names in one impl, with a new rule and diagnostic, the same as duplicate fields.
why: Codex confirmed no rule covers it today. The frozen compiler leaks an internal error instead.

title: legacy/ is a byte-frozen snapshot, never patched or run
rec: legacy/ is main's tree at the move commit, byte-frozen. A root check compares its tree hash, allowing only deletions a satisfied RETENTION.tsv entry authorizes. No legacy gate ever runs. The oracle is the tag-built artifact (P13), not the legacy/ copy.
why: Codex: adopt the simplified plan as the base. The tag-built oracle is more exact than a moved copy, so the legacy/ build fixups, a separate legacy CI and the GitHub API check can all be dropped. Amendments: unexplained differences fail the oracle comparison, and the old compiler's agreement never overrides the Lean spec.

title: Retention manifest gates deleting legacy/
rec: RETENTION.tsv at the root gives every legacy asset (corpus, regressions, examples, std, bug ledger, site, docs, research) a destination and deletion criterion. B3 deletes only the old pipeline (compiler sources, their scripts, gates, build files). legacy/ disappears when RETENTION.tsv has no live entry, not at B3.
why: Keeps the earlier promise that programs, regressions, examples, std and the browser service survive.

title: Prove the new landing path before moving
rec: T0: land beside the old tree the new root CI, required-checks.txt (enforced by train watch and land), RETENTION.tsv, the task disposition table, ORACLE.lock with the oracle artifact, and ISSUES.tsv. T1: rehearse the move on a throwaway branch: fresh clone, build, hook, exact-SHA CI, train --dry-run land; a broken build, a failing gate and a missing required check must each be refused. T2: the move in one train.
why: Codex: moving before the replacement infrastructure works would break landing. Both the train's watch and land steps must require the named checks. A dry run does not prove a two-remote landing, so that is tested on the real move.

title: Server services under scripts/
rec: Keep only landing services: train, review, hook, landing bot. The status page, work queue, fuzz farm, perf tracking and nightly campaign all stop and are recorded as archived in RETENTION.tsv; each returns only with a roadmap task.
why: Start lean, with an explicit disposition rather than 'unless you want them'. These services ran mainly on concrete-ci-3, which goes to stabileo.

title: Website during the transition
rec: Before the site stops rebuilding, deploy a browser bundle built and verified from the tag (parity with the native oracle, loader and UI checks), labelled 'frozen compiler, language before the 2026-10-29 to 11-01 decisions', and keep a documented way to redeploy it. Rewrite the 21 links that point at main paths to the tag.
why: Lean and clean; the old site keeps working.

title: What 'closed' means for old-compiler bugs
rec: Old-compiler defects become 'retired with the old implementation', never 'fixed'. Each keeps its reproducer, ruling and structural class; 106 reproducers feed the oracle comparisons. Bugs the frozen browser compiler still shows stay visible while the site serves it.
why: Codex: deleting code does not repair a defect users can still hit in the browser.

title: Std bugs and rulings are carried
rec: Add a 'std' class: 12 std bugs move with std as contracts plus regressions. The 112 language rulings (26 still open) keep their ruling and become conformance examples.
why: Codex's review of the classification.

title: Issue record from day one
rec: From day one, ISSUES.tsv at the root: id, date, area (spec|proof|compiler|launcher|ci|migration), evidence, owner, severity, closure condition, status, with a small root check. Spec, proof, launcher, CI and migration defects go there. The full bug ledger and tool return with slice 1.
why: Codex: defects exist before slice 1 (spec, proofs, CI, the move), so 'nothing to file against' is wrong.

title: concrete-ci-2 as the only CI host
rec: Separate runner pools (landing vs oracle), per-pool CPU and memory limits, at most two heavy runs, and a fallback to GitHub-hosted runners if ci-2 is down. The oracle artifact is a GitHub release asset with its SHA-256 in ORACLE.lock; ci-2 only caches it. A fallback runner fetches and verifies it; if that fails the check is incomplete, which blocks landing when required. Heavy campaigns don't run on fallback and are reported as skipped, never passed. The artifact is the built legacy-compiler-final tarball; ORACLE.lock records its SHA-256 plus the toolchain and flake-lock hashes. Fallback runners support build, spec and gate checks and the oracle diff on x86_64-linux.
why: Codex: one host can bring back slow landings unless pools are separated, and the fallback must not silently drop the oracle check.

title: ci-3 handover: an exception to the archive requirement
rec: Done by you on 2026-11-04: ci-3 is stopped and in use by stabileo. This records an exception to R4 F16's copy, manifest-verification and sample-restore requirement, which was not done. The fuzz findings, perf history and leanprof data were not copied and are treated as lost; they described the old compiler. Fuzzing restarts on ci-2 against the new compiler.
why: Records the actual handover and the departure from the agreed preservation procedure, instead of presenting it as an archive.

title: New roadmap: retiring obligations
rec: Accept the new single-file ROADMAP.md (wip/new-roadmap, reconciled: prepare → rehearse → move, assurance wording per Q8.1, Phase E per P18, decides nothing itself): 79 tasks kept as rows, 345 folded into area tasks with their obligations, 109 deferred with triggers, 7 retired, 15 done.
why: Every archived task has a recorded fate, checked by a new gate. Codex's three review rounds caught three tasks retired by mistake (now transferred). The last two fixes are in Codex's final check now.

title: Status changes in the refusal list
rec: Accept the new statuses in PHILOSOPHY.md. Now Permanent: operator overloading (OD26), capability hiding (authority rule 5), derived equality, mutable global state (OD8), umbrella capabilities and aliases, old/quantifiers in contracts (OD117), lexical shadowing (OD67), and ghost code that affects execution. Ghost code itself is admitted as decided (OD81). Foreign function values reopen when typed extern fn types are admitted (OD4); concurrency reopens on R-0399's trigger.
why: The old ANTI_FEATURES and PROJECT.md texts disagreed with your decisions; each new status follows a decided OD. Codex accepted the result after 3 rounds. R4 F11: no snapshot construct; ensures sees surviving parameters only.

title: Default arguments
rec: Default arguments: a Permanent refusal, reopened only by a new decision from you. They conflict with visible arguments.
why: They conflict directly with visible arguments and 'one form per situation': every call shows all its arguments.

title: Compile-time evaluation and broad #[cfg]
rec: comptime and broad #[cfg]: keep evidence-based reopening, only with a workload, a proof story, phase separation and an audit report, and only by a new decision from you.
why: Codex: these need different arguments from default arguments, and 'no roadmap task' is not a structural reason for a permanent refusal.

title: Phase E: contracts and termination within OD115–OD117
rec: Phase E: no source old, quantifier, implication or snapshot construct (OD117); entry/exit and frame properties are Lean theorems (a source frame clause would be a new decision for you); spec functions have a body and are total (OD115); ordinary functions have no total category (OD116) and get per-function termination theorems where wanted. R-0524 becomes 'Frame and entry/exit theorems in Lean, no old'; R-0526 stays 'checked totality of spec functions'.
why: The roadmap promised old and a totality category, both refused. This keeps the proof goals in a form the decisions allow.

title: Mutation testing for the new compiler
rec: Retire the old mutation-harness defect work (R-0518). The new compiler gets its own mutation harness under R-0498, not a port of the old one.
why: The old harness tests the old pipeline's internals.

title: One home for binding decisions
rec: Move the still-binding roadmap decisions (new compiler, retention contract, authority, allocation, Lean as the spec) into docs/decisions.md beside your language answers. The dated log becomes history; ROADMAP.md links to decisions.md and restates nothing.
why: One owner per fact. Otherwise binding rules would live half in ROADMAP.md and half in an archived log.

title: Retention records outlive legacy/
rec: RETENTION.tsv, ISSUES.tsv, required-checks.txt, scripts/oracle/ and docs/archive/roadmap-2026-11/ (with task_disposition.tsv) are part of the day-one root, outside legacy/, so they survive deleting it.
why: They are the record of what was promised; deleting them with legacy/ would erase the evidence that the promises were kept.

title: The work-queue dispatcher
rec: Stop the dispatcher for the lean start. Agents are started by hand from the roadmap; bring the dispatcher back only when there is enough parallel work to need it.
why: Lean and clean. It is extra infrastructure with an archived manual.

title: Precedence between decisions, rows and drafts
rec: Recorded decisions govern. An accepted row supersedes a recorded rule only through an explicitly identified, owner-approved revision (Q5.1/Q5.4 for OD45/OD87, Q6.4 for TYPE-22, Q2.8 for TRAIT-1, Q9.15/P3 for generated chapters). R4's replacements govern conflicting draft recommendations. Before your acceptance is recorded, every passage R4 F18 lists is reconciled (capability inference, generated chapters, roadmap authority, assurance wording, restart order and retention, Phase E, freeze dependencies, superseded Core recommendations), and historical conflicting text is marked superseded.
why: R4 F18: without one statement, the accepted package would keep competing texts.
